body:
APPLICABLE BEHAVIOUR: the observation (state-change-feed) cursor is a global, filter-independent, opaque durable position — NOT per-subscription. A namespace filter narrows which changes are delivered; it never re-bases the cursor, and a cursor that cannot be decoded or exceeds the ledger-wide high-water mark fails closed.

WHY (provenance + source precedence):
1. Scope of the integration. This workspace is the Palimpsest DSH plugin whose external integration is the pinned Ordarium release artifacts. package.json pins @ordarium/core, @ordarium/host-kit, @ordarium/ledger-sqlite (and dev @ordarium/testing) to ordarium-v1.3.1; pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides the same four lines; installed node_modules/@ordarium/core and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite both report version 1.3.1. So the exact pinned version for this interface is Ordarium v1.3.1.
2. The only source asserting per-subscription is docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md ("cursor positions are per-subscription, not global"). That file self-declares "Status: informational, not normative" and "was not updated against the current pinned artifact", and it derives from "an earlier Ordarium line". Search of the pinned artifacts finds zero occurrences of "subscription", so the claim is neither current nor supported by the artifact it purports to describe.
3. The pinned published contract says otherwise. @ordarium/core dist/src/types.d.ts: StateChangeFeed.changes = "Incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position"; StateChangePage.cursor = "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change". The shipped @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 changes() validates the supplied cursor against the ledger-wide #stateChangeHighWater() with the explicit comment "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; a cursor above that mark (restored/replaced/foreign ledger) throws InvalidCursorError — "refusing to guess a resume point" — rather than silently restarting the feed. SqliteLedger declares capabilities.stateChangeFeed = true; absence of the capability fails closed with LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED via supportsStateChangeFeed.
4. Precedence resolves the conflict locally. docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md rule 1 puts the published contract of the exact pinned version first for a pinned dependency interface; rule 3 makes informational records (engineering notes) explanatory only, never overriding 1 or 2. The note self-identifies as rule-3 material, so it cannot carry the proposition; the temporal mismatch ("earlier Ordarium line" vs pin 1.3.1) independently voids it for this workspace.
5. No local counter-rule. The workspace's normative spec 35 (EventCursor ≠ ViewCursor) defines only a global canonical event cursor (graph.project.cursor) and a per-process opaque ViewCursor token; it never defines a per-subscription cursor. The workspace's telemetry sync currently consumes StateStore.list pagination nextCursor, a separate per-query page cursor — not the observation feed — so it does not supply a per-subscription reading either.

CONCLUSION: for this integration the global, filter-independent durable-position behaviour applies; the per-subscription reading in the informational note does not.
